notes: All data retrieved 2026-10-06. PLANETS: semi_major_axis_au, eccentricity and longitude_of_perihelion_deg are JPL 'approximate positions' Table 1 J2000 values (Earth row = Earth-Moon barycenter). Mars ϖ is listed by JPL as -23.94362959 deg and was normalised to 0-360 (336.05637041). orbital_period_days = NSSDC sidereal orbit period; mean_radius_km = NSSDC volumetric mean radius; mass_earth = NSSDC mass(10^24 kg)/5.9722, rounded to 5 significant figures (NSSDC's printed ratios agree to their precision). MOON COUNTS: The NSSDC overview fact sheet is stale (Jupiter 95, Saturn 274, Uranus 28, last updated Mar 2025); the counts used come from the JPL SSD discovery-circumstances list of IAU-recognized satellites and NASA science.nasa.gov moon pages (updated Sept 2026), which agree. Jupiter's 115 has no explicit 'as of' date on the NASA page; the IAU said 101 on 26 Mar 2026, so the jump to 115 occurred between then and Sept 2026 (exact MPC date not verified). Third-party sites quote other figures (e.g. Saturn 292) — not used. Counts change often; recheck before release. MOONS: a, e, sidereal period from JPL SSD mean elements (epoch 2000-01-01.5, except Nereid: NEP105, epoch 2020-01-01). Mean elements are averages and e is given to only 3 decimals (e.g. Deimos, Triton, Proteus show 0.000 meaning <0.0005). Earth's Moon elements are JPL's DE405/LE405 ecliptic mean values. mass_kg = JPL GM / G with G = 6.67430e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 (CODATA 2018), 4 significant figures. Uranian moon GMs (URA111) are only ~2-3% precise; Amalthea ~5%; Deimos ~3%. Proteus mass set to null: JPL GM 2.58 ± 2.42 km^3/s^2 (≈94% uncertainty, essentially unconstrained). Nereid mass null: JPL lists GM 0 (unknown). Nereid radius 170 ± 25 km and Hyperion radius (irregular body, 135 ± 4 km) are uncertain mean values; Phobos/Deimos/Amalthea/Hyperion/Proteus are irregular, radius is volumetric mean. retrograde: only Triton (inclination 157.3 deg to Laplace plane) is retrograde among those listed.
